sections.overview: The African Skimmer is a waterbird of broad rivers, lakes and lagoons across sub-Saharan Africa.
sections.identification: Its orange bill has a lower mandible longer than the upper one, a distinctive adaptation for skimming the water surface.
sections.habitat: It forages over calm, shallow water and uses exposed sandbars along rivers and lakes, especially for nesting.
sections.diet: It catches small fish by flying low and dragging its lower mandible through the water; it can close its bill when it contacts prey.
sections.behavior: Outside the breeding season, African Skimmers may gather in large flocks; seasonal movements follow river and lake systems.
sections.reproduction: It lays its eggs in shallow scrapes on bare sand, often in small colonies; both parents incubate and care for the young.
sections.ecology: Breeding is timed to low water, when exposed sandbars provide nesting ground beside feeding areas.
sections.conservation: BirdLife lists the global population as Least Concern, but the species is assessed as Not Applicable in South Africa, where it remains very scarce.
